whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Sales Foundations exam for?

personas.label: Sales representatives who use Salesforce
personas.description: You manage deals in Salesforce and want to show that you know the main sales tools.

personas.label: Sales managers
personas.description: You lead a team that uses Salesforce and want to understand its pipeline and forecasts.

personas.label: People moving into sales operations
personas.description: You support a sales team and want to learn how its sales process works in Salesforce.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Sales Foundations Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This entry-level exam covers both Salesforce and the sales process. It asks how a deal moves from lead to close, what pipeline information means, and which Salesforce tool supports each step. It does not require configuration or coding.
bullets: 40 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
70% to pass, which is 28 correct answers out of 40.
Sales process and Salesforce tools. Expect questions about both selling and the features that support it.
Pipeline and forecasting. Learn what opportunity stages and forecast categories mean.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: You are ready when you can follow a deal from lead to close in Salesforce and explain what a pipeline report shows. Aim for at least 80% on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Sales Foundations Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Questions cover everyday sales work and the Salesforce features that support it.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a sales representative’s task, such as logging a call or following up on a stalled deal, then ask which Salesforce feature to use.
bestWayToPass: Follow a deal from start to finish: Review leads, qualification, conversion, opportunities, products, and closing. Know what each record represents.
Learn pipeline terms: Understand stage, probability, close date, amount, and forecast category.
Review sales tools: Know how tasks, events, email logging, mobile, and Kanban help representatives.
Read reports: Practice explaining what a pipeline report and a simple dashboard show.

certificationCard.description: This entry-level exam covers everyday sales work in Salesforce: leads and opportunities, the pipeline, forecasting, activity tracking, and sales reports. The exam is 40 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 70% pass mark, weighted towards Deal Management (37%) and Planning (21%).

keyConcepts.h2: Sales Foundations: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Leads, Accounts, Contacts, and Opportunities
blocks.body: A **Lead** is a potential customer who has not yet been qualified. When the lead is ready, you can **convert** it to create an **Account** (the company), a **Contact** (the person), and usually an **Opportunity** (the potential deal). Conversion is a one-way step, so do it when the lead is qualified. An Account can be linked to many Contacts and Opportunities, which helps track ongoing business. Know which record holds each kind of information.

blocks.heading: The Pipeline and Forecast Categories
blocks.body: An **Opportunity** has a **stage** that shows its progress, an **amount**, and a **close date**. Stages have a **probability**, and open Opportunities together make up the pipeline. A **forecast category** groups stages into groups such as Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, and Closed. Managers use these categories to estimate what may close in a period. Keep close dates current so the pipeline gives a useful view of expected sales. Move deals to the next stage when they make real progress.

blocks.heading: Activities and Sales Productivity
blocks.body: A **Task** is a to-do, while an **event** is a calendar item such as a meeting. Both can be linked to a Lead, Contact, Account, or Opportunity so the activity history stays with the record. Emails can be logged automatically to make conversations visible to the team. The **Kanban** view lets representatives move Opportunities between stages. **Path** shows guidance and required fields for a stage. The Salesforce **mobile app** supports work away from a desk. **Chatter** lets a representative ask questions on a record and keep the replies with the deal.

blocks.heading: Products, Quotes, and Sales Teams
blocks.body: You can add **products** to an Opportunity from a **price book**, which lists products and their prices. A **quote** can be created from those products and sent to the customer. An **opportunity team** records who is working on a deal and what each person does. Larger deals may need approval before a discount is offered. This exam focuses on knowing what each feature is for, not on configuring it.

blocks.heading: Reports, Dashboards, and Forecasts
blocks.body: A **report** lists or summarizes records, such as open Opportunities expected to close this quarter. A **dashboard** displays information from several reports as charts on one screen. **Forecasting** rolls Opportunity amounts up through the team so managers can estimate what may close. **List views** show a filtered list of records on a tab. Be ready to choose between a filtered list, a summary, a visual overview, and a sales projection.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Sales Foundations Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions describe a sales representative’s work and ask which Salesforce record or feature fits the task.

blocks.heading: Leads and Conversion
blocks.body: A Lead is an unqualified prospect. Converting it creates an Account and Contact, and usually an Opportunity. Conversion cannot be undone.

blocks.heading: Opportunity Management
blocks.body: The stage, amount, and close date describe a deal in the pipeline. Forecast categories group stages for sales projections.

blocks.heading: Activities
blocks.body: Use Tasks for to-dos and events for meetings. Link them to a record so the activity history stays together.

blocks.heading: Reports and Dashboards
blocks.body: Reports list or summarize records. Dashboards show information from several reports. List views give a filtered list of records.

blocks.heading: Teams and Quotes
blocks.body: Opportunity teams record who is working on a deal. Products and price books describe what is being sold; quotes present those products and prices to a customer.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on your sales foundations knowledge with these related Salesforce credentials:

sampleQuestions.question: A sales rep gets a business card from someone who is mildly interested but not yet qualified. Which record should they create?
options: Opportunity
Lead
Account
Quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use a Lead for a person who may become a customer but has not been qualified yet.
whyWrong: An Opportunity represents a potential deal; there is no qualified deal yet.
An Account represents a company the business works with.
A Quote is a priced offer, which comes later in the sales process.

sampleQuestions.question: A Lead has been qualified and there is a real deal to pursue. What can converting the Lead create?
options: A Quote and signed Contract, but no Contact
An Account and Contact, plus an optional Opportunity
An Account and Contact, but no Opportunity
A Case and Task, not a sales Opportunity
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lead conversion creates or links an Account and Contact. It can also create an Opportunity if there is a deal to pursue.
whyWrong: A Quote and Contract usually come later in the sales process.
A converted Lead can create an Opportunity when one is needed.
Cases and Tasks are not the records created through Lead conversion.

sampleQuestions.question: Which three fields show where a deal is in the sales pipeline?
options: Stage, amount, and close date
Lead source, industry, and rating
Billing address, phone, and website
Case origin, priority, and status
sampleQuestions.explanation: Stage shows the deal’s progress, amount shows its value, and close date shows when it is expected to close.
whyWrong: These describe the Lead’s source and the company, not the deal’s progress.
These are company details, not pipeline fields.
These are Case fields used in customer support.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager wants to see what is likely to close this quarter. Which feature can help?
options: Activity timeline
A list view of all Accounts
Forecasting with categories
Lead queue
sampleQuestions.explanation: Forecasting groups Opportunity amounts by category, such as Commit and Pipeline, to show expected revenue.
whyWrong: An Activity timeline shows what happened on a record.
An Account list does not show expected revenue from deals.
A Lead queue holds Leads that need to be worked.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep has just called a Contact and wants the call history saved on the record. What should they do?
options: Log the call as an activity on the Contact record
Create a new Lead for the same person
Write it in a personal notebook, outside Salesforce
Change the stage on the related Opportunity to record the call
sampleQuestions.explanation: Logging a call as an activity attaches it to the Contact so others can see the history.
whyWrong: The person already has a Contact, so creating another Lead could duplicate them.
A private note is not saved for the team on the Salesforce record.
Changing a stage does not record the call.

sampleQuestions.question: Which view lets a rep move Opportunities between stages by dragging them?
options: A report that summarizes Opportunities
The Salesforce Setup menu for administrators
The Kanban view
A dashboard that displays Opportunity charts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Kanban shows Opportunities as cards by stage, and users can drag cards as deals progress.
whyWrong: Reports display and summarize data, but they do not move records between stages.
Setup is for configuring Salesforce, not moving Opportunities between stages.
Dashboards display charts; they do not update records.

sampleQuestions.question: How are an Account and a Contact related?
options: They are two names for the same record
Accounts are only for service, and Contacts are only for sales
A Contact contains many Accounts
Account represents a company; Contacts represent its people
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Account represents a company, and its Contacts represent people linked to it.
whyWrong: Accounts and Contacts are different record types.
Both objects can be used by sales and service teams.
An Account can link to many Contacts, not the other way around.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep wants to add products and prices to a deal. What should they use?
options: A Chatter post describing each product and its price
A Task on the Account to list the products being sold
A new Lead record for every product on the deal
Add Price Book products to the Opportunity
sampleQuestions.explanation: Add products and prices from a Price Book to the Opportunity as line items.
whyWrong: Chatter is for team discussion, not for adding product line items.
Tasks track work to do; they do not add products to a deal.
Leads represent prospects, not products.

sampleQuestions.question: Three colleagues are working on one large deal, and the company wants to record their roles. What should it use?
options: An Opportunity Team with roles
A Case for each colleague
Three separate Opportunities for one deal and three reps
Convert the Lead three times
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Opportunity Team records the people helping with a deal and their roles.
whyWrong: Opportunity Teams record team members and their roles on one deal.
Cases track customer service issues.
Three Opportunities would make one deal appear as three deals.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager wants one screen with pipeline by stage, deals closing this month, and team results. What should they create?
options: A Quote with the monthly pipeline figures
A Dashboard built from reports
A single standard List View with all the records
A Price Book with products for the sales team
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Dashboard can show charts from several reports together on one screen.
whyWrong: A Quote is a priced offer to a customer.
A List View shows a filtered record list, not the requested set of charts.
A Price Book stores product prices.

sampleQuestions.question: Why should reps keep Opportunity close dates accurate?
options: They set the Account owner
They change the product price
They create a Case automatically
Forecasts and pipeline reports use them
sampleQuestions.explanation: Close dates place deals in the right time period for pipeline reports and forecasts.
whyWrong: Account ownership is managed separately.
Prices come from product and Price Book settings.
Close dates do not automatically create support Cases.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep asks a product question and wants the answer saved with the deal for the team to see. What should they use?
options: Chatter on the Opportunity
A personal Task
Change the Account name
A private email
sampleQuestions.explanation: Chatter on the Opportunity keeps the discussion with the deal so teammates can find it.
whyWrong: A Task tracks work to do; it is not a discussion.
Changing the Account name does not answer the question.
A private email is not visible to colleagues unless it is logged.

sampleQuestions.question: In sales forecasting, what does the forecast category indicate about an opportunity?
options: Controls which users can sign in to Salesforce
Groups Opportunity stages into forecast categories
Sets the Account owner for each sales rep
Sets prices for products in a Price Book
sampleQuestions.explanation: Forecast categories group Opportunity stages so managers can separate expected revenue from earlier pipeline.
whyWrong: Login access is controlled through user access settings.
Account ownership is a separate field.
Product prices are set through Price Books.

sampleQuestions.question: A rep needs Salesforce records while visiting a customer without a laptop. What should they use?
options: Salesforce is not available away from a desktop
A personal spreadsheet
Salesforce mobile app
A printed report from last month
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce mobile app lets a rep view records and log work while away from a computer.
whyWrong: Salesforce has a mobile app for phones and tablets.
A personal spreadsheet is not the shared source of current Salesforce data.
A printout can become outdated and cannot be updated from the visit.

sampleQuestions.question: What best describes a pipeline report?
options: A directory of employees
A history of all past invoices
Open Opportunities grouped by stage
A list of closed Cases
sampleQuestions.explanation: A pipeline report groups open Opportunities so users can see each deal’s stage.
whyWrong: An employee directory is not a sales pipeline.
Invoices are billing records, not open sales deals.
Cases are customer service records.
